newsitem.title: FRANCE: Givenchy names Alexander McQueen as designer.
newsitem.headline: Givenchy names Alexander McQueen as designer.

text.p: French fashion house Givenchy on Monday named Britain's Alexander McQueen as its new designer to succeed John Galliano, appointed earlier in the day at Christian Dior.
"Today, Alexander McQueen becomes Givenchy's new designer, and in this capacity he will create the haute couture and luxury ready-to-wear," the house said in a statement.
McQueen, 27, will present his first collection for the more than 40-year-old house next January. He will continue to design for his London-based label while working at Givenchy.
"His creative talent combine with his technical virtuosity will enable McQueen to continue the renewal of Givenchy's image while respecting its tradition of elegance," the statement said.
Both Givenchy and Christian Dior are owned by luxury giant LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton.
